analysis.title: US Equity Strategy Outlook 2027: After the derating, how to invest
key_insights: 2026 was a year of regime shifts. The S&P 500 forward P/E fell about 20% (LTM P/E down about 17% YTD) while 2026 EPS is on track to grow about 33%. Drivers: AI monetization, financing and regulatory concerns, a spike in yields and credit spreads, Iran escalation and higher oil, growth worries, and lower net buybacks.

In years following a >10% fall in the SPX LTM P/E, SPX returned an average 17% and a median 20%, with few negative years. The P/E recouped almost 30% of the prior decline the following year. Exceptions were 1973-74 and 2021-22.

UBS forecasts SPX EPS of $430 in 2027 (+18%) and $490 in 2028 (+14%). NVDA, MU and AVGO alone account for about 45% of 2027 SPX earnings growth. Semis and hardware are over 57% of the $600bn+ rise in 2027 SPX earnings.
SPX target for end-2027 stays at 8900, about 18x 2028 EPS of $490 and about 21% above current. The end-2028 target is 9600 on 17.5x EPS of $550 in 2029. The 2026 target was reduced to 7900.

Midterm results add risk: state-level data center pauses put about 30% of expected 2028 US data center capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas. The earnings hit is hard to size until policy details emerge next year. UBS trimmed 2028 Tech and ex-Tech EPS growth and says risks are skewed lower.

AI demand is accelerating. Annualized q/q cloud revenue growth nearly tripled to about $86bn in Q3 from about $31bn in Q1, on a roughly $540bn run rate. UBS analyst cloud revenue estimates are about 15% above consensus for the next four quarters. Consensus has dollar growth flat from about $140bn in 2H27.

UBS puts AI revenue potential at about $2.5tr in 5 years at the midpoint, excluding next-gen products. This is above the $2tr low hurdle needed to earn a return on $6-8tr of cumulative 2025-30 capex. Including next-gen products the range is $1.4-5.1tr, midpoint about $3.3tr.

Semis rose about 2x in H1 2026 then fell nearly 40% in H2. AI Exposed Semis P/E is about 10x, a roughly 40% discount to SPX. Semis P/E is down about 45-57% depending on the measure. UBS buys Semis over Tech Hardware, whose forward sales CAGR is about 10% versus about 32% for Semis.

Software is overweight. About 85% of market cap is AI net beneficiaries. P/E to sales CAGR has halved to about 1.1x, near 15-year lows. Sales CAGR is about 20%, the highest in over a decade. HOLT forecasts large-cap Software CFROI at a decade high of 18% in 2027.

NDX over RTY is a higher-conviction view. NDX forward EPS has risen about 2x more than RTY's, yet NDX P/E is back near 2022 lows. NDX has about 30% CFROI versus about 10% for RTY, plus median net cash. Chip-based forecasts point to about 51GW of new data center capacity in 2027 versus about 27GW this year.

Hyperscalers are favored because they own scarce compute. Power constraints could leave a 62GW gap by 2030 versus chip-implied capacity. Capacity limits held back core cloud growth at MSFT and AMZN in Q3. Neoclouds fund externally and are squeezed. Moratoriums and grid-upgrade rules raise costs more for new sites than for existing ones.

Growth+CFROI at a Discount (UBEQHGCD) is favored over Expensive Fundamentals (UBEQEXFN). It trades at 16x P/E versus 21x, with a 14% forward sales CAGR versus 5%, 33% CFROI versus 6%, and a PEG on sales CAGR of 1.1x versus 3.8x. The CFROI spread is in the 99th percentile since 2004 while the P/E spread is in the 43rd.

Healthcare is the most attractive sector and tops REVS rankings with an 18% CFROI. Healthcare P/E to sales CAGR is about 3x versus over 6x for Staples. UBS is underweight Staples, its highest-conviction reversal trade, calling the roughly 12% rally in the last month an unwind of a consensus funding trade.

Energy exposure is reduced after a roughly 40% YTD rally. It screens richest versus fundamentals. UBS expects eventual Iran de-escalation and lower oil, and says even higher energy prices would hurt future demand.

Financials are the top cyclical overweight. They screen among the cheapest sectors versus fundamentals even after new highs. Clarity on stress capital buffer rules could lift payouts above consensus. Industrials fall to neutral, Materials rise toward neutral. Discretionary ex-AMZN, Utilities, REITs and Staples are funding sources or underweights.

Rates stay higher for longer. UBS economists expect two more Fed hikes. Rates vol should fall if the Fed hikes twice, and when the Fed hiked under 100bp within a year of rate spikes, SPX rallied 18% on average the next year. AI debt issuance competes with government borrowing, pressuring weaker borrowers. UBS is underweight the High Leverage basket and favors Real Rates Higher over Rate Cut Winners.

Net buybacks fell about $120bn from Q1 to Q3. Hyperscalers swung from about $120bn a year of net buybacks to net issuing about $150bn annualized. UBS expects a $200-400bn rebound in net buybacks next year as OCF and FCF ex-hyperscalers are up $400-500bn y/y. MU, NVDA and AVGO buybacks are expected to reach $422bn by 2028 from $83bn in 2026. Q1 is seasonally strongest.

Valuation framework: above-trend EPS growth pressures the multiple. Since 1984 the SPX forward P/E has fallen about 4% per 10pp of NTM EPS growth above the roughly 6.5% trend, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027. Offsetting this, big deratings tend to partly reverse and SPX ex the big semis trades below its model-implied P/E. UBS assumes the P/E holds near 18x.

OECD CLI regime probabilities: expansion and slowdown are both just below 40%. UBS fades the slowdown and expects AI-led growth to extend the expansion in 2027, with a slower 2028 buildout as the main risk. Rate-sensitive sectors (Cap Goods, Banks, Utilities, Consumer Durables, Real Estate) have underperformed the ML model's implied returns.

Thematic baskets: AI Exposed Semis (UBXXSEMA) and Memory are the top scorers. AI Software Pioneers (UBXXAISP) is the preferred software basket. Longevity & Wellness (UBEQLGWL) is the preferred Healthcare basket. Quality Capital Providers (UBEQQCAP), US Infrastructure over Consumer Cyclicals, and GLP-1 Winners are also favored. AI Power and AI Robotics remain under pressure on valuation.

earnings_insights: UBS forecast (not reported): SPX 2027e EPS $430, +18% y/y following about 33% adjusted growth in 2026. Ex-Tech earnings are expected to grow about 9% and Tech about 30%, down from over 50% in 2026.

UBS forecast: SPX 2028e EPS $490, about +14% y/y and in line with consensus. Ex-Tech is forecast to grow about 8% and Tech about 19%. The end-2028 target uses 2029e EPS of $550, with 12% growth assumed for 2029.
UBS forecast: NVDA, MU and AVGO account for about 45% of the $600bn+ rise in SPX earnings in 2027. NVDA adds $150bn+, MU $90bn+ and AVGO $30bn+. Large backlogs support visibility.
SPX NTM EPS is about 40% above its long-run trend. SPX NTM earnings are set to rise 15%+. Forward 3-5 year sales growth expectations are the highest since before 2003.

UBS expects MU, NVDA and AVGO buybacks to rise to $422bn by 2028 from $83bn in 2026. SPX net buybacks are expected to rise $200-400bn next year. Nvidia and Micron alone could run at over 25% of total LTM US buybacks.

Hyperscalers' net buybacks swung from about +$120bn a year to net issuance of about $150bn annualized in Q2-Q3 as capex outpaced FCF. UBS says issuance remains an overhang if 2027 capex reaches $1.8tr.

trade_ideas.description: Long Semis / short Tech Hardware (AI Exposed Semis basket UBXXSEMA, funded with Tech Hardware)
trade_ideas.rationale: Semis P/E has collapsed to price a fall in profits while forward sales CAGR is about 32% versus 10% for Tech Hardware.
trade_ideas.risk: AI capex slowing, data center pauses, and negative Semis sentiment.

trade_ideas.rationale: NDX EPS revisions are about 2x stronger than RTY, NDX P/E is near 2022 lows, and RTY is more exposed to tighter financial conditions.
trade_ideas.risk: Sharply lower rates for good reasons and AI disappointment.

trade_ideas.description: Long Growth+CFROI at a Discount basket (UBEQHGCD) versus Expensive Fundamentals basket (UBEQEXFN)
trade_ideas.rationale: About a 22% P/E discount for 2.5x the sales growth, with a 1.1x PEG versus 3.8x.
trade_ideas.risk: Growth and CFROI rolling over, though compressed P/E spreads already discount it.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Healthcare funded by Staples (Longevity & Wellness basket UBEQLGWL)
trade_ideas.rationale: Healthcare P/E to sales growth is about half of Staples', and it tops REVS with 18% CFROI.
trade_ideas.risk: Staples could keep rallying as a defensive or consensus trade.

trade_ideas.description: Long Software, AI Software Pioneers basket (UBXXAISP)
trade_ideas.rationale: P/E to sales CAGR near 15-year lows as sales CAGR rises to about 20%.
trade_ideas.risk: Disruption debate for the roughly 15% of market cap at risk, and valuation as a headwind in REVS.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Financials (Quality Capital Providers basket UBEQQCAP); cyclicals over bond proxies
trade_ideas.rationale: Supportive valuations, solid earnings, and a possible payout lift from stress capital buffer clarity.
trade_ideas.risk: Sentiment overhang and a rates spike.

trade_ideas.description: Real Rates Higher basket (UBXXRRHI) over Rate Cut Winners (UBXXCUT); underweight High Leverage basket (UBEQHLEV)
trade_ideas.rationale: Rates are expected to stay high, and Rate Cut Winners has the weakest earnings change score of the thematic baskets.
trade_ideas.risk: A sharp fall in rates for good reasons.

trade_ideas.description: Reduce Energy exposure after a roughly 40% YTD rally
trade_ideas.rationale: Screens richest versus fundamentals, and UBS expects eventual de-escalation and lower oil.

risk_factors: AI capex slowing, or AI demand and capex disappointing, leading to recession and 6.5% unemployment (UBS scenario 4).
A further spike in yields, including a 10-year at 6.5% forcing the Fed to 5.5% and a 2028 recession (scenario 3).
Data center pauses and moratoriums after the midterms put about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk. The earnings impact is hard to size.
Iran escalation, including Brent at $150 adding 1.5pp to CPI and keeping the Fed higher.
Above-trend EPS growth tends to pressure the P/E, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027 and 3% in 2028.
AI prices could fall faster than usage rises, slowing lab revenue before enterprises adopt at scale.
Continued net issuance by hyperscalers if capex reaches $1.8tr next year.
Power is the binding constraint, with a 62GW gap by 2030 on the power-constrained path.
Lower oil is the main risk to the Discretionary underweight, as it would help the consumer.

vol_and_positioning: Rates vol jumped to extreme levels in 2026 and should fall if the Fed hikes twice.
Positioning is described as full earlier in 2026 and sharply reduced in Semis after the selloff. UBS calls the backdrop highly volatile and increasingly driven by positioning and technicals.
Staples rallied about 12% in the last month, which UBS reads as an unwind of a consensus funding trade.
Cyclicals versus defensives did a near 180 in 2026, with H1 outperformance nearly fully reversed as yields spiked.
Momentum composition churned toward Biotech and Healthcare after the June derisking. Sentiment and crowding readings improved for Software.
geopolitical: Iran conflict was a key driver of oil, rates and equities in 2026. UBS sees escalation as a risk but eventual de-escalation as the end point.

US midterm election results: Democratic sweep and governor-elects supporting pauses or moratoriums on new data center construction, putting about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk, including 18GW in Texas.
Middle East conflict and higher oil prices added to derating pressure and to the rise in yields.

tension_points.theme: semis derating vs data center pauses
tension_points.bull_case: Semis P/E near 10x already prices mean reversion, AI demand is on the steep part of the S curve, backlogs support 2027 EPS, and a slower buildout could extend the cycle and ease financing pressure.
tension_points.bear_case: State-level data center pauses put about 30% of 2028 capacity additions at risk, and the earnings hit is hard to size. UBS says 2028 risks skew lower.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of disappointing AI demand data points or ~50GW of 2027 deployment not materializing; UBS says it would adjust views if evidence of accelerating AI adoption into H1 2027 does not appear.

tension_points.bull_case: After >10% P/E falls SPX returned a median 20% and the P/E recouped about 30% of the decline. SPX ex big semis trades below the model-implied P/E.
tension_points.bear_case: Above-trend EPS growth tends to compress the multiple, pointing to a 4-5% derating in 2027. 1973-74 and 2021-22 saw derating continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further yield spike (10-year at 6.5%) or AI capex slowing would invalidate the bull case.

tension_points.theme: cyclicals vs defensives under high rates
tension_points.bull_case: AI-led growth extends the expansion, Financials are cheap, and rate-sensitive industries overshot the ML model's implied returns.
tension_points.bear_case: The yield spike and a slower 2028 AI buildout pose risks, and expansion and slowdown probabilities are both near 40%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Incoming macro data showing the backdrop has firmly shifted into slowdown, per the OECD CLI regime probabilities.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers fund the build from operating cash flow, own scarce compute, and cloud revenue growth should stabilize FCF.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscalers net issued about $150bn annualized in Q2-Q3, and issuance remains an overhang if capex reaches $1.8tr next year.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ~50GW deployed on the chip path in 2027 would break the scarcity position because it would clear demand loose instead of tight.
